There are several "YouTube Analytics MCP" (Model Context Protocol) servers available on GitHub, each catering to different use cases.

### Key Options
*   **CData YouTube Analytics MCP Server:** A professionally maintained, read-only server that leverages CData JDBC drivers to connect Claude Desktop to YouTube Analytics data[1][2]. It is designed for enterprise-grade performance and schema-aware context[3][4].
    *   **Repository:** [CDataSoftware/youtube-analytics-mcp-server-by-cdata](https://github.com/CDataSoftware/youtube-analytics-mcp-server-by-cdata)[1][5]
*   **Open-Source / Community MCP Servers:** There are several community-driven projects that focus on direct OAuth2 integration, allowing you to connect Claude Desktop to your private YouTube Analytics data without third-party drivers[6][7].
    *   **Example Repository:** [dogfrogfog/youtube-analytics-mcp](https://github.com/dogfrogfog/youtube-analytics-mcp) (or similar variants)[8][9]. These often emphasize features like audience demographics, traffic sources, and video performance metrics[8][9].
    *   **Developer-focused:** Some repositories like `itsadityasharma/youtube-channel-data-mcp` are specifically highlighted by users for providing direct, local-only access to private channel data[6][7].

### How to Choose
*   **For Enterprise / Reliability:** The **CData** implementation is generally recommended if you require stable, supported infrastructure and are already using or familiar with CData drivers[1][4].
*   **For Personal / Free Usage:** The **open-source community servers** are better suited if you want a free, self-hosted, and transparent way to query your own channel data using your own Google API credentials[6][9].

### Important Considerations
*   **Security:** If you use community-built servers, ensure you review the code to understand how your credentials (API keys/OAuth tokens) are handled[9].
*   **Setup:** Most community-driven servers require you to create a project in the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), enable the YouTube Analytics/Data APIs, and manage your own `credentials.json` file[9].

Several MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers have been developed to integrate YouTube Analytics with AI assistants like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others[1][2][3]. These allow you to query your private channel data using natural language[4][5][6].

Below are the most relevant GitHub-related resources and implementations:

### Key MCP Servers for YouTube Analytics
*   **[CData Software](https://github.com/CDataSoftware/youtube-analytics-mcp-server-by-cdata):** Provides a read-only MCP server that connects Claude Desktop to YouTube Analytics via CData JDBC drivers[7][8][9]. It is designed for enterprise-grade data access and integrates with their broader Connect AI platform for CRUD support[7][10][4].
*   **[pauling-ai/youtube-mcp-server](https://github.com/pauling-ai/youtube-mcp-server):** A comprehensive open-source project built with Python and FastMCP[11]. It is noted for being one of the few that covers three distinct YouTube APIs (Data API v3, Analytics API, and Reporting API), supporting channel performance, audience insights, and SEO discovery[11].
*   **[i1s-abhishek/youtube-studio-mcp](https://github.com/i1s-abhishek/youtube-studio-mcp):** A local, Python-based MCP server that allows for both reading analytics and managing YouTube Studio tasks (such as updating video metadata, posting comments, and uploading thumbnails)[3].
*   **[adityaarsharma/youtube-marketing-skills](https://github.com/adityaarsharma/youtube-marketing-skills):** Part of an agent-agnostic YouTube growth toolkit that includes live channel MCP support[2]. The creator also highlighted an open-source MCP server specifically for private YouTube Analytics[5][6].

### General Setup Requirements
Most of these servers follow a similar configuration process:
1.  **Google Cloud Console:** You must create a project and enable the **YouTube Data API v3** and **YouTube Analytics API**[12][11][3].
2.  **Authentication:** You will need to generate OAuth 2.0 Client ID credentials (usually in a JSON file)[12][3].
3.  **Local Execution:** These servers typically run locally on your machine, ensuring your private credentials and analytics data do not leave your system[12][3][6].

If you are looking for a specific repository, the search terms `"youtube-analytics-mcp"` will primarily point you toward the **CData** implementation[7][9] or various community-maintained projects like those listed above[2][11][3].

The search results indicate that these three terms refer to different implementations of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers designed to interact with YouTube data.

### **1. YouTube Analytics MCP Server by CData**
*   **Source:** [CDataSoftware/youtube-analytics-mcp-server-by-cdata](https://github.com/CDataSoftware/youtube-analytics-mcp-server-by-cdata)[1][2]
*   **Purpose:** A read-only MCP server that allows AI models (like Claude Desktop) to query live YouTube Analytics data[3][4].
*   **Mechanism:** It uses CData JDBC Drivers to expose YouTube Analytics data as relational SQL models[3][4]. This allows users to ask natural language questions about their data without needing to write SQL queries[3][5].
*   **Usage:** It is intended for local hosting[6][7]. CData also offers managed alternatives (CData Connect AI) and other beta servers for users requiring full read/write/update/delete capabilities[1][6].

### **2. pauling-ai/youtube-mcp-server**
*   **Source:** [GitHub - pauling-ai/youtube-mcp-server](https://github.com/pauling-ai/youtube-mcp-server)[8]
*   **Purpose:** A comprehensive MCP server that covers the YouTube Data API v3, Analytics API, and Reporting API[8][9].
*   **Features:** Provides approximately 40 tools for various tasks, including channel analytics, video publishing, transcript management, audience insights, SEO discovery, comments, and bulk reporting[8][9].
*   **Requirements:** Built with Python and FastMCP; it requires users to provide their own Google Cloud OAuth credentials[8][10]. Note that analytics access generally requires the YouTube channel owner's account[11].

### **3. youtube-studio-mcp**
*   **Source:** [i1s-abhishek/youtube-studio-mcp](https://github.com/i1s-abhishek/youtube-studio-mcp)[12][13]
*   **Purpose:** A local MCP server focused on YouTube metadata, thumbnails, comments, and analytics[12][14].
*   **Integration:** It is often associated with workflows involving AI agents (such as Codex or Claude Code) to automate channel management tasks like uploading videos, updating titles/descriptions, and reviewing comments[15][16].
*   **Installation:** Can be installed via `pip install youtube-studio-mcp`[17].

The **YouTube Analytics API** allows you to retrieve performance data for your channels and videos by combining **metrics** (the measurements of activity) and **dimensions** (the criteria used to aggregate that data).

### **Key Metrics**
Metrics are the quantitative data points you can request. The ones you mentioned are standard supported metrics:

*   **`views`**: The number of times your videos have been viewed (a core metric).
*   **`estimatedMinutesWatched`**: The total number of minutes that users have watched your videos. Note that while you mentioned "watchTime," the API specifically uses `estimatedMinutesWatched` for this data.
*   **`estimatedRevenue`**: The total estimated revenue (in USD) from all sources, including ads and YouTube Premium.
*   **`averageViewDuration`**: The average length, in seconds, of video playbacks.
*   **`subscribersGained`**: The number of subscribers gained.

Other common metrics include `likes`, `dislikes`, `shares`, `comments`, and `subscribersLost`.

### **Key Dimensions**
Dimensions are the attributes used to slice or group your metric data. Common dimensions include:

*   **`day`**: Aggregates data by date.
*   **`video_id`**: Aggregates data by individual video.
*   **`country_code`**: Aggregates data by the viewer's country.
*   **`channel_id`**: Aggregates data by channel.
*   **`age_group`** and **`gender`**: Useful for demographic breakdowns.

### **How to Use Them**
When querying the API, you must specify at least one metric and typically one or more dimensions to organize the data.

*   **API Structure**: Every request to the YouTube Analytics API requires you to define these parts in your query string (e.g., `metrics=views,estimatedMinutesWatched` and `dimensions=day`).
*   **Data Availability**: Most data is available with a 48–72 hour delay.
*   **Documentation**: For the full, up-to-date list of all available fields and their definitions, you can always refer to the official [Google for Developers YouTube Analytics API documentation](https://developers.google.com/youtube/analytics/).

Building an automated YouTube video production pipeline using Python involves orchestrating several powerful tools to handle everything from content acquisition to final export[1][2].

### The Core Technology Stack
*   **Content Acquisition:** `yt-dlp` is the industry standard for downloading YouTube videos or extracting audio[3][4][5].
*   **Transcription:** `OpenAI Whisper` provides highly accurate, local, and private speech-to-text transcription[6][7].
*   **Media Processing & Assembly:** `MoviePy` (powered by `FFmpeg`) is the primary library for cutting clips, adding transitions, layering audio, and exporting the final video[8][9][6][10].
*   **Image Processing:** `Pillow` (PIL) is used for creating or manipulating thumbnails, overlays, and other visual assets[8][11].

---

### Typical Automated Pipeline Architecture
Most developers structure their pipelines as a series of modular Python scripts (or a single class-based pipeline) that pass data from one stage to the next[2][12]:

1.  **Ingestion/Scripting:**
    *   Use `yt-dlp` to download raw source material (e.g., footage from Twitch/YouTube)[13][4].
    *   Use an LLM (like OpenAI's API or local models like Llama 3) to generate video scripts or summarize content[3][1][12].
2.  **Audio Processing:**
    *   Use `Whisper` to transcribe the downloaded audio[6][7].
    *   Use Text-to-Speech (TTS) libraries (like `edge-tts` or `gTTS`) to generate voiceovers if you are creating new content[8][14][12].
3.  **Visual Composition:**
    *   Use `Pillow` to generate dynamic text overlays, title cards, or watermark images[8][15].
    *   Use `MoviePy` to assemble the final sequence, applying effects like the "Ken Burns" zoom/pan, cross-fades, and synchronization of voiceover with video clips[8][13][16].
4.  **Export & Deployment:**
    *   `FFmpeg` (invoked via `MoviePy` or `subprocess`) handles the heavy lifting of encoding and final rendering[8][6].
    *   YouTube Data API v3 is typically used to automate the final upload and metadata (title, description, tags) management[2][12].

---

### Implementation Tips
*   **Modularity:** Build your pipeline in small, independent modules (e.g., `download.py`, `transcribe.py`, `edit.py`)[2][12]. This makes it easier to debug and swap out components (like changing your TTS provider) later[2].
*   **Local Processing:** Running `Whisper` locally on a GPU (if available) avoids API costs and keeps your data private[7]. On AMD hardware, consider `whisper.cpp` with a Vulkan backend for better performance[7].
*   **Performance:** For long-form content, render in segments or use `FFmpeg` directly for complex concatenation to avoid the memory overhead that `MoviePy` can sometimes encounter with very long projects[6][12].
*   **Environment Management:** Always use `virtualenv` or `conda` to manage your dependencies, as `MoviePy`, `Whisper`, and `FFmpeg` require specific versions and system-level binaries[17][6][12].

args.Message:
# Comprehensive Research Report: YouTube Analytics MCP & Python in YouTube Production Workflows

---

## Part 1: YouTube Analytics MCP (Model Context Protocol)

### 1. What is YouTube Analytics MCP?
**YouTube Analytics MCP** is a **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server** designed to bridge AI systems (such as **Antigravity IDE**, **Claude Code**, **Claude Desktop**, **Cursor**, etc.) directly with Google’s **YouTube Analytics API** and **YouTube Data API v3**. 

By standardizing access via MCP, AI assistants can query, analyze, and manage a YouTube channel's private performance metrics, viewer demographics, content metadata, and channel management tasks directly through natural language queries in the agent interface.

---

### 2. Major Implementations Found on GitHub & Web
Our search across GitHub and developer communities identified several prominent implementations of YouTube MCP tools:

1. **`CDataSoftware/youtube-analytics-mcp-server-by-cdata`** (Enterprise Read-Only):
   - **Overview:** Maintained by CData Software. Uses CData JDBC drivers to expose YouTube Analytics as relational SQL tables.
   - **Use Case:** Provides Claude/AI agents with schema-aware, read-only SQL querying capabilities over channel analytics.
2. **`pauling-ai/youtube-mcp-server`** (Comprehensive Open-Source):
   - **Overview:** Built in Python using `FastMCP`. Connects to 3 Google APIs: YouTube Data API v3, Analytics API, and Reporting API.
   - **Features:** Exposes ~40 tools covering analytics, video publishing, transcript management, audience insights, and SEO discovery.
3. **`i1s-abhishek/youtube-studio-mcp`** (Local Management & Studio Automation):
   - **Overview:** Python-based package installable via `pip install youtube-studio-mcp`.
   - **Features:** Integrates analytics with active studio operations—updating video titles/descriptions, uploading thumbnails, fetching video stats, and listing/replying to comments.
4. **Community Open-Source Repositories** (e.g., `dogfrogfog/youtube-analytics-mcp`, `adityaarsharma/youtube-channel-data-mcp`):
   - **Overview:** Lightweight OAuth2 servers for creators wanting private, local-only access to their channel data without 3rd-party dependencies.

---

### 3. What Data & Actions It Exposes

#### **A. Key Analytics Metrics**
- **Engagement & Traffic:** `views`, `estimatedMinutesWatched`, `averageViewDuration`, `averageViewPercentage`, `impressions`, `impressionClickThroughRate` (CTR).
- **Monetization:** `estimatedRevenue`, `cpm`, `rpm`.
- **Subscriber & Feedback Dynamics:** `subscribersGained`, `subscribersLost`, `likes`, `dislikes`, `comments`, `shares`.

#### **B. Key Analytics Dimensions**
- **Temporal:** `day`, `month`.
- **Content:** `video_id`, `playlist_id`.
- **Audience & Geography:** `country_code`, `age_group`, `gender`.
- **Technology & Traffic:** `device_type`, `operating_system`, `traffic_source_type` (e.g., YouTube Search, Suggested Videos, External, Browse Features), `sharing_service`.

#### **C. YouTube Studio Actions** *(Available in Read-Write implementations like `youtube-studio-mcp`)*
- Video metadata retrieval and update (`title`, `description`, `tags`, `category`).
- Thumbnail uploading and verification.
- Transcript/subtitle retrieval.
- Comment listing, filtering by sentiment/question, and automated draft replying.

---

### 4. How to Set It Up

Setting up a YouTube Analytics MCP server generally follows these 5 steps:

#### **Step 1: Create a Google Cloud Project**
1. Go to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. Create a new project (e.g., `youtube-mcp-analytics`).

#### **Step 2: Enable Required APIs**
In the GCP API Library, search for and enable:
- **YouTube Data API v3**
- **YouTube Analytics API**
- *(Optional)* YouTube Reporting API

#### **Step 3: Create OAuth 2.0 Credentials**
1. Navigate to **APIs & Services > Credentials**.
2. Configure the **OAuth Consent Screen** (User Type: External / Internal, add test user email).
3. Create credentials: **OAuth Client ID** -> Application type: **Desktop App**.
4. Download the JSON credential file as `client_secret.json`.

#### **Step 4: Perform Initial Authorization**
Run the MCP server script locally for the first time. It will open a browser window requesting Google OAuth authentication. Log in with the account owning the YouTube Channel. This generates a local `token.json` containing access and refresh tokens.

#### **Step 5: Register MCP Server in AI Environment**
Add the server configuration to your AI client's configuration file (e.g., `claude_desktop_config.json`, Antigravity `mcp_config.json`, or Cursor settings):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "youtube-analytics": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["-m", "youtube_studio_mcp"],
      "env": {
        "YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE": "C:/path/to/client_secret.json",
        "YOUTUBE_CHANNEL_ID": "UCxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

### 5. How a Creator Uses YouTube Analytics MCP in Agentic AI Workflows (e.g., Antigravity, Claude Code)

In an agentic environment like **Antigravity IDE** or **Claude Code**, an AI agent isn't just answering questions—it has active tool use capabilities. Here is how creators leverage it:

1. **Automated Weekly Channel Audits & Anomaly Detection:**
   - *Prompt to Agent:* "Check my video performance over the last 14 days. List any video where the CTR is below 4.5% or retention drops below 30% in the first minute."
   - *Agent Workflow:* Agent calls `get_video_analytics` via MCP -> processes metrics -> flags underperforming videos -> proposes 3 new titles and thumbnail concept revisions.

2. **Retention-Informed Scripting & Content Strategy:**
   - *Prompt to Agent:* "I'm drafting a new 20-minute video script on Python async/await. Look at the retention curves and average view durations of my previous 3 Python tutorials via YouTube Analytics MCP."
   - *Agent Workflow:* Agent queries past video retention patterns via MCP -> notes that code demos without voiceover caused retention drop-offs at min 5:00 -> advises restructuring the new script to place interactive diagrams at min 4:30.

3. **Live A/B Testing & Metadata Optimization:**
   - *Prompt to Agent:* "I updated the thumbnail and title on video ID `abc123xyz` 48 hours ago. Compare the CTR and impressions before and after the change."
   - *Agent Workflow:* Agent queries daily dimension analytics -> calculates relative CTR lift -> suggests keeping or reverting changes.

4. **Automated Audience Sentiment & FAQ Extraction:**
   - *Prompt to Agent:* "Fetch the latest 200 comments on my latest long-form video. Categorize them into Bugs reported, Feature requests, and Praises, and draft replies for unresolved technical questions."

## Part 2: How Python Fits Into a Long-Form YouTube Content Creator's Workflow

Python serves as the **operational backbone** for tech, educational, and commentary creators. Rather than relying on manual GUI clicks across multiple applications, long-form creators use Python scripts to automate every phase of the 6-stage production lifecycle:

```
[1. Pre-Production & Research] ➔ [2. Audio & Script Alignment] ➔ [3. Video Processing & Assembly]
                                                                              │
[6. Repurposing & Shorts]     └─ [5. Publishing & Metadata Sync] ◄─ [4. Automated Thumbnails]
```

### Stage 1: Pre-Production, Competitor Research & Scripting
- **Competitor & Trend Scraping:**
  - Creators use `yt-dlp` and `google-api-python-client` to scrape video titles, view counts, and publish dates of top competitors.
  - Scripts use `youtube-transcript-api` to pull full text transcripts from competing viral videos.
  - Python sends transcripts to LLM APIs (`google-genai` / OpenAI) to extract common hooks, content gaps, and high-frequency keyword clusters.
- **Automated Script Outlining & Spoken Duration Estimation:**
  - Python scripts parse raw markdown scripts, count spoken words, calculate estimated video run-time based on average speaking pace (e.g., 140 words/min), and insert timestamp markers for B-roll transitions.

### Stage 2: Audio Cleaning & Subtitle Alignment
- **Offline AI Transcription & Subtitle Generation:**
  - Creators use `openai-whisper` or `faster-whisper` in Python to transcribe raw voiceover audio locally.
  - Python formats word-level timestamps into `.srt` / `.vtt` caption files and automatically extracts major topic shifts into YouTube Chapter timestamps (e.g., `00:00 - Introduction`, `03:45 - Installation`).
- **Audio Normalization & Silence Stripping:**
  - Using `pydub`, `soundfile`, or `ffmpeg-python`, scripts analyze speech audio waveforms.
  - Automatically strips pauses longer than 0.6 seconds and normalizes audio volume to YouTube’s standard **-14 LUFS** loudness target.

### Stage 3: Post-Production & Video Editing Automation
- **Automated Rough Cuts & Dead-Air Removal:**
  - Python scripts inspect raw footage using `ffmpeg-python` or `MoviePy` to detect silence or mistake takes, cutting out dead space before footage enters Non-Linear Editors (NLEs).
- **Programmatic Motion Graphics & Code Renderings:**
  - For coding channels, Python scripts use `PIL` (Pillow) + `MoviePy` or `Manim` (Mathematical Animation Engine) to programmatically generate animated code syntax highlighting, callout boxes, and lower-third graphics directly into `.mp4` video files.
- **NLE Scripting Integration (DaVinci Resolve / Premiere):**
  - Advanced creators use DaVinci Resolve’s built-in Python API (`DaVinciResolveScript`) to automate project creation, timeline generation, color-grading preset application, and batch rendering exports.

### Stage 4: Dynamic Thumbnail Generation
- **Automated Frame Extraction & Graphic Compositing:**
  - Scripts use `opencv-python` to inspect raw 4K video files and automatically select high-quality candidate frames based on sharpness, lighting, and facial expressions.
  - Python passes selected frames through background removal libraries like `rembg`.
  - Using `Pillow` (PIL) or `Cairo`, Python overlays high-contrast text, drop shadows, color borders, and channel logos to render 1280x720 PNG thumbnails in batch.

### Stage 5: Publishing & Metadata Synchronization
- **One-Click Video Upload & Metadata Sync:**
  - A single Python CLI script reads project assets from a folder (`final_video.mp4`, `thumbnail.png`, `script.json`, `chapters.txt`).
  - Uses `google-api-python-client` to upload the video to YouTube Data API v3, assign title, description, tags, playlist ID, set publish schedule, upload thumbnail, and insert video chapters.

### Stage 6: Content Repurposing (Long-Form ➔ Shorts) & Custom Analytics
- **AI-Powered Vertical Clipping (Shorts/Reels):**
  - Python scripts take long-form 16:9 videos and use `Whisper` transcripts + LLM logic to pinpoint 30–60 second viral segments.
  - Python uses `mediapipe` + `opencv-python` to track the speaker’s face in 16:9 video and dynamically crop/reframing it to 9:16 vertical format.
  - `MoviePy` burns word-by-word animated captions onto the center of the vertical video.
- **Custom Analytics Dashboards & Performance Alerts:**
  - Creators run Python scripts (`pandas`, `plotly`, `matplotlib`) connected to YouTube Analytics API to generate custom lifetime decay curves, RPM revenue trackers, and subscriber retention models.
